When GCP resources managed by Config Connector stop reconciling or wedge on deletion — inspect *.cnrm.cloud.google.com objects for UpdateFailed, DependencyNotReady, ManagementConflict, DeleteFailed/stuck finalizers, and generation drift. Degrades explicitly on clusters without Config Connector installed.

MCP tool: `k8s_state_kcc`

## Usage

```sh
lookout state kcc [flags]
```

## Common flags (every `lookout` command)

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` | string | — | limit the scan to one namespace |
| `-A` | bool | — | scan all namespaces |
| `--workload` | string | — | target one workload as \<Kind>/\<namespace>/\<name>, e.g. Deployment/prod/api |
| `--since` | duration | — | how far back to look (0 = command default) |
| `--format` | string | `logfmt` | output format: logfmt\|json (one record per line either way) |
| `--timeout` | duration | `10s` | abort the invocation after this long (exit 1) |
| `--kubeconfig` | string | — | path to a kubeconfig file, instead of $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config |
| `--kubeconfig-dir` | string | — | directory of kubeconfig files to fan out across (mutually exclusive with --kubeconfig); each finding is stamped with cluster=\<label> and the summary reports clusters=\<n> |
| `--context` | string | — | kubeconfig context to read, instead of its current-context. Selects a cluster for THIS invocation only — nothing is written back — so concurrent invocations can target different clusters. Reported as context=\<name> in the summary line |
| `--contexts` | string | — | comma-separated kubeconfig contexts to fan out across, or '*' for every context in the selected kubeconfig(s) (mutually exclusive with --context); each finding is stamped with cluster=\<label> and the summary reports clusters=\<n> |
| `--concurrency` | int | `4` | maximum concurrent cluster executions when fanning out with --contexts or --kubeconfig-dir |
| `--exemptions` | string | — | path to a git-reviewed exemption file (YAML); covered findings are ANNOTATED with their reason and expiry and counted as exempt=\<n> in the summary, never dropped |

## Finding kinds

Every `kind=` this command can emit, and the severities it carries them at. Nothing else appears in its output; a kind absent from a run means the check looked and found nothing. See the [finding-kind glossary](/reference/finding-kinds/) for the whole vocabulary.

| Kind | Severity | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kcc.not_ready` | warning, info | a Config Connector object is not Ready, stuck terminating, or has an unreconciled spec generation |
| `kcc.unavailable` | info | no Config Connector (*.cnrm.cloud.google.com) CRDs are served by the cluster, so nothing was examined (no coverage lies) |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## Output fields

Beyond the shared envelope fields (`kind`, `severity`, `namespace`, `kind_of_object`, `name`, `reason`, `message`, `fingerprint`, `exempt_reason`, `exempt_expires`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `gvr` | GroupVersionResource of the Config Connector object (group/version/resource) |
| `api_version` | apiVersion of the Config Connector object |
| `condition_reason` | the Ready condition's reason reported by the Config Connector controller |
| `observed_generation` | status.observedGeneration last reconciled by Config Connector |
| `generation` | metadata.generation of the object |
| `age` | how long the object has been terminating (DeletionBlocked) or existed |
| `unavailable` | summary-line note when Config Connector CRDs are not installed (kcc-not-installed) |
| `resource` | read.unavailable: the resource that could not be read, as resource[.group] |

## Output contract

Output: one finding per line (logfmt; --format=json for one JSON object
per line), keys in fixed order; healthy resources emit nothing. The final
line is always the summary: scanned=<n> findings=<n> elapsed=<d> —
findings=0 with a summary present means "scanned and healthy"; a stream
without a summary line is void. Exit 0 data, 1 runtime error (diagnostics
on stderr only), 2 usage.

## Examples

```sh
lookout state kcc
lookout state kcc --namespace=prod
lookout state kcc --format=json
```
